answer.q: What should landowners know about forestry mulching in the Texas Hill Country?
answer.a: Forestry mulching in the Texas Hill Country grinds cedar, brush and trees in place on thin, rocky soil without pushing that soil around. Slope, rock and density set the pace and decide the machine. Root balls stay in the ground to hold the soil, and a fine finish lets grass regrow faster.

sections.h2: Forestry mulching on Texas Hill Country limestone
paras: The Texas Hill Country is the southeastern edge of the Edwards Plateau, bounded on the east and south by the Balcones Escarpment. The region takes in counties such as Comal, Kendall, Blanco, Hays, Kerr, Gillespie and Bandera, and it is cut by the Guadalupe, Blanco, Pedernales and Medina rivers.

Soil across most of the Hill Country is thin and rocky over limestone. A dozer disturbs that thin soil and raises the risk of erosion. A forestry mulcher grinds standing growth, leaves root balls in place, and leaves the soil where it lies.

Loose surface rock on Hill Country land can be put to work. Our [on-site rock crushing in Central Texas](rock-crushing) processes existing surface rock into a fine, compactible road base, so less material has to be trucked in.

sections.h2: Cedar brakes, oak mottes and mesquite flats
paras: Hill Country vegetation grows in patterns. Ashe juniper, called cedar locally, forms dense brakes on canyon slopes and spreads into open ground. Live oaks and Spanish oaks gather in mottes and along draws. Mesquite and mixed brush take over flatter pastures and old fields.

Selective forestry mulching works with those patterns. We take the cedar and brush you want gone and leave the oaks and open ground you want kept. Drought stress and oak wilt are common in Central Texas, and selective clearing is often the best option to protect healthy trees near a declining one. For Ashe juniper specifically, see [cedar removal in Texas](cedar-removal).

sections.h2: Mulch depth and how fast Hill Country grass returns
paras: Grass comes back fastest under light mulch, often within days after a rain. Heavy timber can leave mulch up to 12 inches deep, and grass under that much material can take 2 to 3 years. Our crews aim for a fine finish, small material they call hamster chips, which lets grass regrow faster than a coarse one.

If you want less material on the ground, mulch can be stockpiled or hauled off. Settle that choice before the job starts, especially on ranch land where grazing is the goal. [Ranch land clearing](ranch-pasture-clearing) is built around reclaiming pasture.

sections.h2: Where we work across the Hill Country
paras: 9 Arrow is based in Spring Branch, in western Comal County, and we work across Central Texas and the Texas Hill Country. We are a service-area business, so the machines come to your land. Compact track machines handle tight access and slopes, and large articulated wheel machines cover open ground with high production.

Local pages cover [forestry mulching in Spring Branch](forestry-mulching-spring-branch-tx) and [cedar removal in Boerne](cedar-removal-boerne-tx). If your property sits somewhere else in the Hill Country, call (210) 247-8410 and ask.

If your land is somewhere else in the region, call (210) 247-8410 and we will tell you if we can get there.

faqs.q: Can a forestry mulcher work on rocky Hill Country slopes?
faqs.a: Yes, a forestry mulcher can work rocky Hill Country slopes when the machine fits the ground. Compact track machines are built for slopes, tight access and uneven ground. Terrain changes the pace, so a smaller machine on steep, rocky ground may cover about half an acre to an acre in a day.

faqs.q: Is forestry mulching a good fit for Hill Country ranch land?
faqs.a: Forestry mulching fits Hill Country ranch land because it opens pasture without stripping thin soil. Cedar and brush are ground in place, root balls stay put, and grass under light mulch can return within days after rain. Old bulldozer brush piles, even ones as large as a house, can be mulched too.
